kjv: he hath set the world in their heart
mine: he has put eternity into man's heart
note: Hebrew ha'olam in biblical Hebrew means "long duration, eternity"; the sense "world" is post-biblical. Some read 'elem "ignorance". The KJV's "world" reflects later usage.

kjv: God requireth that which is past
mine: God seeks what has been driven away
note: Hebrew nirdaf is "the pursued/persecuted" (or "what has passed by"); the KJV interprets it as past time being called to account.

kjv: the spirit of man that goeth upward
mine: whether the spirit of man goes upward
note: MT vocalises ha'olah and hayyoredet with the article ("that goes up / that goes down"), as the KJV does, probably to avoid doubting the afterlife; the LXX, Vulgate and syntax favour the interrogative "whether ... whether", making it a question about human destiny. Context: a question: who knows whether ... whether (medium confidence). The consonants allow the interrogative ha- 'whether', read by the LXX (ei), Vulgate (si) and most modern versions and suiting the doubt of 3:19-22. But MT points it as the article ('that goes up'), and 12:7 'the spirit returns to God' shows the book does not deny an ascent, so the question is favoured, not certain. Other possible meanings: (1) 'Who knows the spirit of man that goes upward, and the spirit of the beast that goes down?' — MT vowels, KJV, NASB, NKJV, much Jewish tradition, implying that man's spirit does rise; (2) the question read as a denial ('no one knows that it rises') rather than as honest uncertainty — some commentators.
